text:
Maria: Heads-up: a few customers report our v4 streaming change is breaking incremental parsers in mobile SDKs. It looks like clients that relied on EOF to detect completion are hanging.

Ashok: Which change exactly? The one where v4 streams a final token `__end_of_stream__` instead of closing?

Maria: Yep. Before we closed the socket to signal the end, now there's an explicit chunk. Older SDKs didn't handle it.

Dina: How widespread is this? Any big customers blocked?

Maria: Two mid-market customers flagged it and our iOS alpha cohort had multiple reproducible failures. Not catastrophic yet but risky.

Kevin: We should avoid forcing SDK updates immediately. Short term: create a lightweight streaming-compat proxy that converts the final token into a normal stream close for callers that opt in.

Samir: Agree. Tradeoffs: added hop and tiny per-connection state to detect the token. We can scope to per-tenant routing for Hosted/Dedicated and make Private opt-in.

Liz: We must ensure billing and token metrics are preserved. If the proxy collapses or masks chunks we still need to emit identical token usage upstream.

Ashok: Implementation idea: proxy streams chunks through; when it sees `__end_of_stream__` it closes client connection immediately. Minimal buffering — don't accumulate messages, only watch for the final token.

Maria: Rough transform pseudocode:
```
if model.startsWith("v4") and (request.header == "X-Redwood-Compat: stream-eof" or old_client_version):
  forward chunks as-is
  if chunk == "__end_of_stream__": close client socket
else:
  passthrough
```

Dina: How will clients indicate they want compat mode? Header? SDK auto-detect?

Kevin: Make both possible: header `X-Redwood-Compat: stream-eof` to force it; auto-enable when `X-Redwood-Client-Version` indicates an older SDK that doesn't support the token.

Samir: Also respond with a deprecation header so clients see a warning: `X-Compat-Warn: streaming-eof-deprecated; removal=2026-10-01`.

Liz: Test plan:
- unit tests for token detection and graceful close
- e2e with iOS alpha SDK behind canary proxy
- load test to measure latency and memory overhead
- billing validation to confirm token counts match upstream

Ashok: Rollout plan suggestion:
- feature-flagged opt-in at 1% of traffic
- monitor for 48h, then 10% if healthy
- 50% after 7 days, then wider if stable
- automatic rollback if error budget exceeded

Maria: Key metrics to monitor: `streaming_close_count`, `compat_proxy_latency_p50/p95/p99`, `billing_token_delta`, `sdk_errors.v4_stream_waiting`.

Samir: Ops note: implement as stateless stream hijack when possible to avoid buffering. If buffering is unavoidable cap it to small size and fail open (pass-through) while incrementing `compat_buffer_overflow`.

Liz: Docs & comms: migration guide for SDKs + customer email explaining temporary compat header and deprecation timeline (6 months). Add sample code for server/webhook workers.

Ashok: CI: add integration tests that run both streaming styles over a corpus of prompts and assert parity of final payload semantics.

Deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: streaming-compat-proxy v1 to cluster-alpha at 2026-06-15T16:00Z :rocket:

Maria: Ownership: I'll coordinate customers and docs. Need infra/ops help for the stateless hook.

Samir: I can implement the hook and tests. Kevin, can you own rollout and dashboards?

Kevin: Yep — I'll add dashboards, SLOs, and a mobile-lab synthetic that checks EOF behavior. Also will add a runbook for rollback.

Dina: Add a temporary Slack alert to #incidents if `sdk_errors.v4_stream_waiting` spikes above 5/min.

Maria: Action items:
- Maria: migration docs & customer comms
- Samir: proxy implementation + tests
- Kevin: dashboards & rollout runbook
- Liz: billing validation & token count tests
- Ashok: SDK header negotiation PR

Maria: ETA for alpha canary? Two weeks?

Samir: Prototype in 5 days; complete tests in 12 days.

Kevin: Dashboards/runbook in 7 days.

Maria: Great. Reconvene next Wed to review results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
